taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 378, Veratrum viride: "Stems stout, 5-20 dm. tall, very leafy".

traits.height_max_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 378, Veratrum viride: stems "5-20 dm. tall".

traits.life_span.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 377, Veratrum: "Tall perennial herbs, with thick short poisonous rootstocks".

traits.woodiness.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 377, Veratrum: "Tall perennial herbs".

traits.perennation.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 378, Veratrum viride: "rootstock erect, 5-8 cm. long, 2.5-5 cm. thick, with numerous fibrous-fleshy roots".

traits.rhizome_habit.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 378, Veratrum viride: "rootstock erect".

traits.rosette.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 378, Veratrum viride: stems "very leafy", the leaves along the stem, with no basal rosette.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Leaves borne singly up the stem, spirally, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 67994916, 392001108, 241925248, 299734528, 390147558, 238421038, 177023123, 135388654): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.leaf_habit.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: the shoots die back to the rootstock each autumn, as the photos' late-season yellowing leaves show.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 378, Veratrum viride: "the lower broadly oval or elliptic", "the upper successively narrower and acuminate".

traits.leaf_apex.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 378, Veratrum viride: "Leaves acute".

traits.leaf_venation.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 377, Veratrum: "the leaves mostly broad, clasping, strongly veined and plaited".

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 378, Veratrum viride: lower leaves "15-30 cm. long".

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 378, Veratrum viride: lower leaves "7-15 cm. wide".

traits.inflorescence.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 378, Veratrum viride: "panicle 2-6 dm. long, the lower branches spreading and more or less drooping".

traits.inflorescence_posture.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 377, Veratrum: key: "Panicle drooping; flowers green. 1. V. viride".

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 378, Veratrum viride: "panicle 2-6 dm. long".

traits.pedicel_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 378, Veratrum viride: "pedicels 2-6 mm. long, mostly shorter than the bracts".

traits.tepal_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 378, Veratrum viride: "perianth-segments oblong or oblanceolate, acute, 8-10 mm. long, woolly-pubescent".

traits.flower_size_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: open flowers 1.5 cm to 2 cm across, about twice the 8-10 mm perianth segments Abrams gives.

traits.flower_colour.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 378, Veratrum viride: "flowers yellowish green"; sRGB by eye from the photos.

traits.sexual_system.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 377, Veratrum: "Flowers greenish, white or purple, rather large, polygamous or monoecious".

traits.fruit_type.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 378, Veratrum viride: "capsule 20-25 mm. long, 8-12 mm. thick, many-seeded".

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 378, Veratrum viride: "capsule 20-25 mm. long".

traits.flowering_months.note: In flower in July and August at Paradise and in the Cascades, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 67994916, 392001108, 241925248, 299734528, 390147558, 238421038, 177023123, 135388654): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: capsules ripe in August and September, after the July and August flowers.

generator.params.note: Set by hand for green false hellebore from Abrams's description and the photos the traits cite, on beargrass's (xerophyllum-tenax) program values: one or two stout stems, very leafy, the broad sheathing leaves largest low on the stem and narrowing upward (Abrams 1923 p. 378), ending in a panicle about a third of the stem's height whose lower branches spread and droop (flower_branches 5, nod 30). Few stems flower in a year and only after several years' growth (adult_age 5, an estimate). Not fitted to measurements. flowering_share 0.4 (beargrass's) removed 2026-10-19: with two stems it left no stem to flower in any year, though Abrams (1923 p. 378) describes every stem as ending in its "panicle 2-6 dm. long"; the melanthiaceae program's own value (every adult stem ends in its inflorescence) now applies.

appearance.organs.leaf.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 377, Veratrum: "the leaves mostly broad, clasping, strongly veined and plaited"; Abrams (1923 p. 378): "sessile or short-petioled, sheathing". Drawn as a broad, sessile, elliptic leaf with strong parallel veins.

appearance.organs.flower.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 378, Veratrum viride: "flowers yellowish green; perianth-segments oblong or oblanceolate, acute". Drawn as a star of six pointed, yellowish green tepals.

appearance.note: By eye, from the photos the traits cite: a tall, stout, very leafy stem of broad, pleated, yellow-green leaves, crowned by a drooping panicle of small yellowish green flowers. Organ cards from common beargrass's (xerophyllum-tenax), recoloured and resized by hand. Colours set by eye were written as screen (sRGB) shades; they are read as the linear light a colour field holds, and bark and foliage follow the stated colour traits by rule (2026-10-19).

allometry.note: 1.3 m tall at 8 years in the open, within its sources' range, as it grows in subalpine parkland. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.
